full_judgment:
2. The opposite party Nos.1-13 as plaintiffs instituted the suit for declaration of their title in the suit land measuring 0.24 acres, as well as recovery of khas possession in respect of a part of the suit land and for a declaration that the Kabala dated 7-6-1986 registered in Bhurungamari Sub-Registry Office in respect of a part of the suit land is illegal, void, inoperative and not binding upon them and on the basis of the said kabala the defendant Nos. 1-3 did not acquire any title in any part of the suit land. 

 5. During trial 7 witnesses were examined on behalf of the plaintiffs and 3 witnesses were examined on behalf of the defendants. After hearing the parties the learned Assistant Judge by his judgment and decree dated 8-8-1986 decreed the suit. On appeal the said judgment and decree were affirmed with some modification. The Appellate Court did not maintain the decree passed by the trial Court in respect of the prayer about the Kabala since the plaintiffs got the decree declaring their title in the suit land and for recovery of khas possession. 

 8. In reply to his such argument Mr Md Sirajul Islam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-opposite parties, submits that the Courts below on proper consideration of the materials on record arrived at the decision that on 5th January 2004 the 'plaintiffs were dispossessed forcibly from a part of the suit land which was under their possession being purchased by their predecessor in 1966 and for such dispossession the plaintiffs prayed for decree for recovery of khas possession, the Courts below with concurrent findings granted such decree. In arriving at their such decision the Courts below also considered the facts that allegedly the plaintiffs were dispossessed on 5th January 1994 and on the next day i.e. on 6th January 1994, there was a Salish in the local police station: Mr Khan further submits that whether the plaintiffs were dispossessed forcibly from a part of the suit land is a question of fact and the Courts below on proper consideration of the materials on record concurrently found that on the date mentioned above the plaintiffs were dispossessed forcibly from a part of the land under their possession which is a part and parcel of 0.24 acres of land purchased by their predecessor from admitted owner Khodeza Khatun in 1966 and for such dispossession no partition suit is necessary. By taking forceful possession nobody acquired any title in any such dispossessed land. In respect of the commissioner report, Mr Khan submits that though the said report Exhibit '1(A)' is not a report submitted by any Advocate Commissioner appointed by the Court but the said Exhibit' 1(A) is a public document supplied by a public office and it is admissible as evidence as per  the provision of law provided in the Code of Civil Procedure. In support of his such contention, Mr Khan cited the decisions reported in contention, Mr Khan cited the decisions reported in AIR 1941 Patna 260,43 DLR 568, AIR 1963 Orissa 11, PLD 1972 Peshawar 175.
